expect.label: < 1 tok/param
expect.meaning: Fewer tokens than parameters — training will likely diverge or severely underfit.

expect.label: 1–10 tok/param
expect.meaning: Usable but significantly undertrained — expect poor generalisation and high loss.

expect.label: 10–30 tok/param
expect.meaning: Chinchilla-optimal zone (Hoffmann et al. 2022) — best loss per FLOP.

expect.label: 30–200 tok/param
expect.meaning: Training smaller models longer reduces inference cost — the LLaMA / Mistral strategy.

expect.label: < 0.5 tok/param
expect.meaning: Likely insufficient for meaningful task adaptation — model may not converge on the target task.

expect.label: 0.5–1 tok/param
expect.meaning: Lower bound for stable full-parameter fine-tuning — expect some instability.

expect.label: 1–5 tok/param
expect.meaning: Standard supervised fine-tuning range for large models — stable and effective.

expect.label: 5–20 tok/param
expect.meaning: Generous dataset — effective, but monitor for catastrophic forgetting of base model capabilities.

expect.label: < 10 tok/adapter_param
expect.meaning: Adapter likely won't converge reliably — insufficient signal for low-rank matrices.

expect.label: 10–50 tok/adapter_param
expect.meaning: Lower bound of the convergence zone — reliable but not yet in the ideal range.

expect.label: 50–100 tok/adapter_param
expect.meaning: Practical sweet spot for task adaptation — strong convergence with low forgetting risk.

expect.label: 100–1000 tok/adapter_param
expect.meaning: Large dataset relative to adapter size — consider increasing LoRA rank or switching to full fine-tuning.
